source.title: A margin-based multiclass generalization bound via geometric complexity
source.authors: Michael Munn; Benoit Dherin; Javier Gonzalvo

record.tranche_reason: The study trains ResNet-18 with original and random labels and reports how geometric complexity relates to excess risk, but it does not directly report the fitting outcomes specified in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a qualitative correlation between geometric complexity and excess risk for training with original and random labels. It does not state that random-label training error reaches zero or that test error is at chance. Figure curves are not reported as numeric values in the text.
record.test_reason: Random-label training is used to evaluate geometric complexity as a generalization measure. The reported outcome is its correlation with the train–test accuracy gap, which does not establish perfect training fit, chance test accuracy, or any other claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report correlated geometric complexity and excess risk under original and random labels, and derive margin-based generalization bounds involving geometric complexity under stated distributional and model assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: ResNet-18 is trained with SGD on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using original and random labels; the reported analysis tracks geometric complexity and excess risk rather than directly reporting random-label fitting outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (CIFAR-10 versus CIFAR-100) and label regime (original versus random) are separate reported conditions; the text describes the correlation in both.

fits_no_version.finding: Geometric complexity correlates with the reported excess risk during original- and random-label training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For ResNet-18 trained with SGD on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, geometric complexity tracks the train–test accuracy gap during training.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The paper reports qualitative correlations but does not provide text values for training error or test error under random labels. The relevant curves are figures without numeric values in the supplied text; no uncertainty or control results are reported for these experiments.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero random-label training error and chance test error. Shared architecture and stated training settings alone do not establish these outcomes.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across intermediate label-corruption fractions.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout and data augmentation on fitting and generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable curve values. It defines excess risk as test accuracy minus training accuracy; that gap does not establish either accuracy separately. Figure 1 also rescales geometric complexity so the random-label curves meet.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not report random-label training error reaching zero or near zero, test error at chance, or whether architecture and hyperparameters were unchanged relative to true-label training.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD using CIFAR-10 original labels; tracked excess risk and geometric complexity during training.
rows.measure: Relationship between excess risk and geometric complexity across training.
rows.value: The geometric complexity is closely correlated with excess risk; the two quantities tend to increase at a comparable rate during training.
rows.note: This reported relationship does not establish the random-label fitting outcomes in V1.
rows.check: The correlation measures a different construct from V1–V6. Appendix D specifies batch size 256, 100,000 steps and learning rate 0.05.
